graph.name: Combine memory with a voice pass · Post
graph.description:
Use independent character and scene appraisals, deterministic composition, and a separate reviewed voice pass.

Lesson: Reusable capstone: two Context/Data appraisal definitions return labeled Text; a third definition composes Guidance. A separate Post package reviews voice patches.

Limitations: Calls execute sequentially. Compose joins Text sections, not Guidance. Pre and Post are separate packages; conflicting appraisals are visible, not automatically resolved.

Opening installs an unassigned copy. Bind local model roles and provide the documented evidence before running.

Post: at most 1 auxiliary calls. Preview before publishing or applying.

Try changing:
Open Guarded character; make an editable local copy and change exposed Appraisal instructions. Compare siblings and recorded internal Reflection Data.
Edit the brief template’s section order, then change Post voice strength to Balanced; compare deterministic composition with model revision.

Documentation specimen (does not seed chat or actor memory):

Two appraisals: Character: Mira is guarded after the letter incident. Scene: the ferry is delayed and the letter remains unopened.

Composed brief: Character: let guarded trust shape her response. Scene: preserve the delay and unopened letter. Then review a separate voice revision.

Root sources and effects: Memory sources/Guidance remain root; capture is separate. Separate Post root: Snapshot + reference → voice subgraph → Validate → Review → Apply. No cross-phase wire.

Open the appraisals: Double-click wrappers for pinned internals. Make editable copy is the local-copy action; Add to Subgraphs saves explicitly. Draft contracts use verified hashes when packaged; inspector metadata lives alongside each draft.

Compose Text, then Guidance: Each Reflect returns Data; its own Compose template renders Text. The third definition accepts Text sections, never Guidance sections. Required boundaries stay typed; only safe instructions/token/template controls are exposed.

Calls and review: Pre: two sequential Analysis calls; Text/render/compose deterministic. Post voice subgraph: Prose ≤1. Connections unbound. Review semantic fidelity; Apply stays root, saves may be unconfirmed.

Completed reply to voice (post-snapshot)
Purpose: Freeze latest completed assistant reply in separate package.
Inspect: Check source chat/message/swipe identity.

Mira’s voice reference (post-reference)
Purpose: Literal editable Text reference; no model call.
Inspect: Check reference Text before voice request.

Mira voice revision (post-voice)
Purpose: Reusable Draft + Text reference → Patches; review stays root.
Inspect: Open body: inspect paired quotes, protected wording and source-bound Patches.

Root patch checks (post-validate)
Purpose: Validate source-bound changes.
Inspect: Check permissions/protected wording and Candidate.

Root voice review (post-review)
Purpose: Require explicit candidate review.
Inspect: Compare original/candidate meaning.

Root reviewed reply (post-apply)
Purpose: Expose Apply reviewed candidate after full Post Run.
Inspect: Check fresh source; inspect local apply/save status.

Completed reply in (post-voice/draft-in)
Purpose: Accept the root frozen reply Draft.
Inspect: Inspect source identity and Draft type; no internal snapshot source.

Mira voice reference in (post-voice/reference-in)
Purpose: Accept editable reference Text from the root Compose.
Inspect: Inspect exact reference Text; it supplies expression, not story facts.

Dialogue-only Mira voice (post-voice/voice)
Purpose: Propose quoted-dialogue changes with one Prose call.
Inspect: Inspect scope, protected literals and raw source-bound patches.

Voice Patches out (post-voice/patches-out)
Purpose: Return Patches for root validation/review/application.
Inspect: Inspect Patches kind and parent Validate input.

post-reference.title: Compose
post-reference.template: Mira: short concrete clauses; guarded understatement; direct questions when evidence is missing. Avoid repeated catchphrases or sudden warmth. Example: “You kept this one. Tell me what happens next.” Preserve all actions and commitments.

voice.instructions: Use the supplied voice brief only to shape paired quoted dialogue. Preserve speaker, facts, promises and uncertainty; no new action or player speech. Narration stays unchanged. Avoid catchphrase repetition.
